name: United Kingdom
tuition: £15,000–£35,000+ a year for international master's students.
living: About £1,100–£1,500 a month; more in London.
postStudyWork: Graduate Route visa after the degree; check the current length.
notes: Most master's degrees are one year, which keeps total cost down.

name: Ireland
tuition: About €15,000–€30,000 a year outside the EU.
living: About €1,200–€1,600 a month; Dublin is dearer.
schemes: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarships
postStudyWork: Stay Back permission (Stamp 1G), up to 2 years after a master's.

name: Germany
tuition: No tuition at most public universities; Baden-Württemberg charges non-EU students €1,500 a semester. A semester fee of roughly €100–€400 applies everywhere.
living: About €1,000 a month; the student visa needs a blocked account of about that much per month.
schemes: Foundation scholarships (Heinrich Böll, Konrad Adenauer and others)
postStudyWork: 18 months to look for work after graduating.
notes: Living costs are the main expense. Many biomedical master's are taught in English.

name: Netherlands
tuition: About €12,000–€25,000 a year outside the EU.
schemes: University excellence scholarships (Leiden, Utrecht, Amsterdam, Groningen, Maastricht)
postStudyWork: Orientation year: one year to find work.

name: Belgium
tuition: Flanders: about €6,000–€12,000 a year outside the EU at some universities, less at others. French-speaking universities: about €4,000, with waivers for some countries.
postStudyWork: A search year after graduating.

name: France
tuition: Public universities: about €3,900 a year for non-EU master's students, often reduced or waived by the university.
living: About €900–€1,300 a month; Paris is dearer.
postStudyWork: A temporary residence permit to look for work after a master's.
notes: Many programmes are in French; check the language of teaching.

name: Italy
tuition: Public universities: from €0 to about €4,000 a year, set by family income.
grants: Regional right-to-study grants (DSU Toscana, DiSCo Lazio, EDISU Piemonte, ER.GO and others): means-tested, can cover fees, housing and meals
postStudyWork: A permit to look for work for up to 12 months.
notes: The regional grants are the big, less-known route: apply in the summer before starting.

name: Spain
tuition: Public universities: about €1,000–€5,000 a year, set by each region.
postStudyWork: A permit to look for work for up to 12 months.
notes: Many master's are taught in Spanish.

name: Portugal
tuition: About €1,000–€7,000 a year outside the EU.
postStudyWork: Time to look for work after graduating.

name: Austria
tuition: Public universities: about €730 a semester outside the EU.
postStudyWork: 12 months to look for work.

name: Switzerland
tuition: Public universities: about CHF 1,500–4,500 a year for foreign students.
living: About CHF 1,800–2,500 a month: one of Europe's dearest.
postStudyWork: 6 months to look for work.
notes: University excellence awards here usually cover living costs too; they are very competitive.

name: Sweden
tuition: About SEK 90,000–300,000 a year outside the EU.
schemes: Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals (needs about 3,000 hours of work experience)
University tuition scholarships (Lund, Uppsala, Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm, Chalmers)
postStudyWork: 12 months to look for work.
notes: Applications for autumn usually close in mid-January.

name: Norway
tuition: Fees for students outside the EU/EEA since 2023: about NOK 100,000–400,000 a year.
postStudyWork: 12 months to look for work.
notes: Few scholarships cover the new fees; check each university.

name: Denmark
tuition: About €10,000–€17,000 a year outside the EU.
schemes: Danish Government Scholarships (tuition waivers through universities)
postStudyWork: Establishment card: up to 3 years after a master's.

name: Finland
tuition: About €8,000–€18,000 a year outside the EU.
schemes: Finland Scholarship (first-year tuition and a grant)
postStudyWork: Up to 2 years to look for work.
notes: Joint application rounds usually open in December and close in January.

name: Iceland
tuition: Public universities charge only a registration fee (a few hundred euros a year).
postStudyWork: Up to 3 years to look for work.

name: Hungary
tuition: About €3,000–€10,000 a year without a scholarship.
schemes: Stipendium Hungaricum (tuition, monthly stipend and housing for partner countries)
postStudyWork: 9 months to look for work.
notes: Stipendium Hungaricum applications usually close in mid-January.

name: Czechia
tuition: Free in Czech; English-taught programmes about €2,000–€10,000 a year.
schemes: Czech Government scholarships for developing countries
postStudyWork: 9 months to look for work.

name: Poland
tuition: About €2,000–€6,000 a year.
postStudyWork: 9 months to look for work.

name: Estonia
tuition: About €4,000–€12,000 a year; some programmes waive fees.
postStudyWork: 9 months to look for work.

name: Canada
tuition: About CA$15,000–40,000 a year for international students.
schemes: Funded thesis-based MSc places (paid from a supervisor's grant)
postStudyWork: Post-Graduation Work Permit, up to 3 years.
notes: Thesis-based (research) MSc places are often funded, but you usually need a supervisor to agree first. Email them early.

name: United States
tuition: About US$20,000–60,000 a year.
postStudyWork: Optional Practical Training (OPT), 1–3 years.

name: Australia
tuition: About A$30,000–50,000 a year.
postStudyWork: Temporary Graduate visa.
